questions.prompt: How do analysts sign in, and should the signed-in analyst's identity be recorded on each approval? (e.g. 'local username+password, record approver' / 'shared login, no identity' / 'SSO')
questions.default: Local username + password accounts held by the app itself; the signed-in analyst's identity is recorded on every approval.
questions.why: Decides whether architecture composes a local auth module (no managed identity service, per the local self-contained deploy target) and whether the data model's approval record carries an approver identity field for the REQ-015 audit trail; also determines how REQ-017's 'analysts only, never anonymous' access rule is enforced on the conversation-history screen.

questions.prompt: How long should conversation records be kept, and must customer PII be redacted before storage?
questions.default: Retain conversations for 90 days, then purge; store customer content as written with no automated PII redaction.
questions.why: Sets the retention window and purge job in the data-design layer and the PII-handling stance in the governance/security report; a 'redact' answer adds a redaction step to the message-persistence path in build-backend, which a 'store as-is' answer omits entirely.

questions.prompt: After an analyst approves a reply, does the app send it to the customer itself (outbound email / ticket-system integration), or does the analyst copy it into the existing email tool?
questions.default: The app does not send anything; on approval it marks the reply approved and the analyst copies it into the existing email tool.
questions.why: Decides whether architecture and build-backend include an outbound delivery integration plus its credentials and send/failure states, or whether approval is a terminal state with a copy-to-clipboard affordance in the frontend; this is the single largest swing in the build budget for this run.
